answer: A karst garden keeps Sybils out through graft pruning. A newcomer grafts 16 trees over 30 days, each graft bound with waxed thread and its new growth measured by 2 gardeners from different groves, logged in the garden register within a day. A tree with no new growth loses its credit and rewards freeze 14 days; three barren trees void the whole count. Faking 1,000 agents takes 16,000 grafts, 32,000 measurements, 30,000 garden-days: $4 a graft, about $64,000 before one reward. A real orchard earns its fruit the way a graft earns its branch, one true shoot at a time.
